drugRefs.dose: Pip-tazo 4.5 g IV q6h + Clindamycin 900 mg IV q8h + Vancomycin 15-20 mg/kg IV q8-12h
drugRefs.duration: Until surgical source control achieved and clinically improving (often 2-3 weeks total)
drugRefs.why: This combination covers polymicrobial type I infection (pip-tazo), provides antitoxin effect against streptococcal/staphylococcal toxin production (clindamycin, via protein synthesis inhibition), and covers MRSA (vancomycin) — maximal reasonable empiric coverage is justified given the extreme mortality risk.

coverageMatrix.completeness: Triple combination covers both type I and type II necrotizing fasciitis patterns comprehensively pending surgical/culture findings.
gaps: Clindamycin resistance in some Streptococcus/Staphylococcus strains exists — does not change the empiric approach but is relevant once susceptibility is known.

stewardship.deescalation: Narrow to the most targeted regimen once intraoperative cultures identify the organism(s) (e.g., confirmed monomicrobial Group A Streptococcus allows narrowing from triple therapy to penicillin + clindamycin); continue until adequate source control and clear clinical improvement.

drugs.drug: IVIG (adjunctive, for confirmed streptococcal toxic shock features)
drugs.coverage: Considered as adjunctive therapy in confirmed streptococcal necrotizing fasciitis with toxic shock syndrome features, in consultation with infectious disease.

framework: EMERGENT surgical exploration and debridement is the single most important intervention — antibiotics do not penetrate necrotic tissue effectively, and delay in surgery directly increases mortality regardless of antibiotic choice.

Maximal empiric coverage is justified here specifically because of the extreme mortality of undertreatment — this is one of the few scenarios where broad empiric triple therapy is the stewardship-correct choice, not an exception to be minimized.

De-escalate promptly once intraoperative cultures identify the organism(s) — the broad initial regimen should not be continued for the full course once a monomicrobial cause (e.g., confirmed Group A Streptococcus) is identified.

references: IDSA Skin and Soft Tissue Infection Guidelines
